name: Notification
summary: A richer, stacking message with a title + description — rendered through antd's notification API.
lead: Notification is antd's imperative `notification` API — a card with a title, description and optional actions that stacks in a corner — and keeps antd's built-in motion, so it stays on real Ant: antd v6 (React) and ant-design-vue v4 (Vue), both themed once by the shared notificationTheme. Two implementations, one DS V3 look. This is the composite half of the hybrid.

spec.label: Type
spec.value: success · info · warning · error (status glyph + tone)

props.name: duration
props.desc: Seconds on screen; 0 keeps it until dismissed

props.name: btn
props.desc: One optional action (e.g. Undo) rendered in the card

whenToUse.when: a message with a title + detail, or one from a background event the user may act on later
a one-line, past-tense confirmation with nothing to act on
the user must respond before continuing

opinion.note: Give it a short title and a one-sentence description. Put at most one action in it; anything more belongs in a Modal or the page itself.
opinion.dsv3: COVERED — antd v6 notification.useNotification() themed by the shared notificationTheme (white card · 384 wide · radius 8), matrix: type {success · info · warning · error} × placement {topLeft · topRight · bottomLeft · bottomRight}, plus duration (0 = sticky) and an optional action btn. The DS forbids the static notification.open()/message() call — only the hook's contextHolder card consumes the ConfigProvider theme; every snippet (HTML/React/Vue) uses the hook. Verified via Figma search_design_system on the DS V3 set (fileKey MwjvUjVI0HnfwD9EwPXRAy): V3 ships no dedicated Notification component set (only Badge lives in V3; Notification remains in v2/Beta), so the DS V3 look is themed antd v6 against the V3 tokens (colorPrimary #6A1EBB, colorError #F5222D, borderRadius 8).

snippets.label: HTML
snippets.note: Composite has no framework-free element, so its paste-and-run form is a CDN-React page — React + antd load from a CDN and mount on open, consuming the same shared notificationTheme. No build step.

codeNote: React and Vue are two real vendor libraries at two Ant generations — they can't share a primitive. They converge via the same notificationTheme; residual drift is caught by visual regression.

conformance.$about: Measured by qa.mjs against the RENDERED UI (getComputedStyle via headless CDP). Composite shown as a CDN-React page; a sticky notification (duration 0) is opened on mount so the measure reads the real antd v6 notification card bound to notificationTheme.
